1. Approval and Contract Documents. Order Approval occurs when the Buyer signs or accepts the order in writing and the Seller confirms acceptance in writing. The completed product table, Commercial Schedule, agreed specifications and these terms form the Contract. Buyer purchase order terms apply only if expressly accepted by the Seller. Changes require written agreement by authorised representatives.

2. Quantity, Price and Value. The goods must meet the agreed grade, specification and measurement basis. Rates apply per stated unit in the contract currency. Quantity tolerances and price adjustments apply only as expressly agreed; no mixed-unit quantity total applies. The final balance is the final agreed invoice total less the advance. Additional charges and taxes must be identified in the commercial terms.

3. Payment Within 24 Business Hours. The Buyer must pay {advance_percentage}% of the total contract amount within 24 business hours of Order Approval. The remaining {balance_percentage}% must be paid within 24 business hours of receipt of the Seller’s written notice that the identified conforming goods are ready for pickup (Ready Notice), and always before release or loading. The Seller may defer procurement, production, allocation and release until the applicable payment clears. Payment is complete only on receipt of cleared funds in the verified nominated account. The Buyer bears transfer charges and must not deduct or set off amounts except where mandatory law requires it.

4. Business Hours and Notices. The 24-business-hour period counts only hours within the business days, opening hours and time zone entered in the Commercial Schedule; it is not automatically one business day. Time starts on receipt of the approval or notice, or at the next opening time if received outside those hours. Use the stated email or another agreed written channel with reliable delivery evidence. Failed delivery is ineffective. The notice must state the actual payment and collection deadlines.

5. Prompt Collection and Charges. The Buyer must arrange pickup as soon as practicable and collect within the completed collection grace period following the Ready Notice. That period does not extend the payment deadline. For Buyer-caused delay, the agreed storage, handling, reheating, reloading and demurrage charges accrue after the grace period. Any penalty or delay compensation requires a completed basis and cap and applies only to the extent lawful. Charges must be reasonable and evidenced, without duplicate recovery. No charge applies for Seller-caused delay or where lawful pickup is prevented by a qualifying force majeure event.

6. Default and Uncollected Goods. The Seller may withhold release, suspend the affected order and give written default notice for late payment or collection. After the completed cure period, the Seller may cancel the unperformed portion and, where lawful, resell or reallocate goods following further notice. The Seller must mitigate loss, credit payments and net resale proceeds against the same debt, and refund any surplus. Only lawful losses and charges may be recovered; the advance is not automatically forfeited.

7. Delivery, Risk and Title. The signed delivery arrangement controls delivery and risk. Unless otherwise agreed, delivery and risk transfer occur when loading onto the Buyer’s suitable vehicle is completed at the agreed pickup point. The Buyer arranges onward transport and insurance. Title passes only after full cleared payment, to the extent lawful. Storage risk for overdue goods passes only where legally permitted, after identification, segregation and written notice; the Seller remains responsible for the legally required standard of care.

8. Packaging and Pre-Dispatch Inspection. Packaging must match the agreed product description. Before dispatch, the Seller’s team and the Buyer’s authorised representative should inspect the goods, bags, pallets and cages as applicable, and record visible defects on the delivery note. The Buyer must arrange a representative and suitable transport equipment. After risk transfer, the Seller is not responsible for damage caused by improper carriage, storage or handling; this does not exclude defects existing at delivery or mandatory rights.

9. Quality, Inspection and Claims. The Buyer must inspect apparent condition, grade identification and quantity before leaving the pickup point and record discrepancies. Signing receipt does not waive latent defects not reasonably discoverable on inspection. Notify latent defects promptly within the completed period after discovery, subject to mandatory rights. Preserve traceability, photographs and representative sealed samples where practicable, and permit reasonable inspection or independent testing before mixing, use, resale or disposal, except for essential safety measures.

10. Remedies and Liability. For proven nonconformity attributable to the Seller, the Seller may remedy, replace the affected goods or refund their price, with return where reasonably required, subject to mandatory law. The Seller is not responsible for post-delivery contamination, overheating, improper handling or use contrary to agreed specifications. To the extent lawful, indirect and consequential losses and lost profit, business or production are excluded; aggregate liability is capped at the price paid or payable for the affected goods. The limits do not cover fraud, wilful misconduct, gross negligence, death, personal injury or any liability that cannot lawfully be limited.

11. Cancellation and Changes. Following Order Approval, cancellation or amendment requires the Seller’s written agreement, subject to mandatory rights. A permitted cancellation may include evidenced, reasonable, nonrecoverable procurement or production costs and other legally recoverable loss after mitigation and credit for resale or reused materials. Apply the advance against the lawful amount owed and refund the excess; no double recovery is permitted.

12. Force Majeure and Regional Conflicts. The Seller is not liable for delay or nonperformance to the extent directly caused by an event beyond its reasonable control that could not reasonably be avoided or overcome. Events include earthquakes, floods, severe storms, wildfire and other natural disasters; epidemics and official restrictions; global or regional war, invasion, armed hostilities, military operations, terrorism, civil unrest, blockade, political conflict, sanctions and government orders; and resulting closure of borders, ports, airspace or transport routes, or interruption of essential utilities, supply or carriage. This includes qualifying events involving or affecting Iraq, the United States of America and other Middle Eastern countries. Actual causal impact must be established; a conflict’s existence alone is insufficient. Ordinary price increases, lack of funds or avoidable failures alone do not qualify.

13. Force Majeure Procedure. The Seller must promptly notify the Buyer, explain the affected obligations, take reasonable mitigation measures, provide material updates and resume when practicable. Affected deadlines extend only for the actual disruption and reasonable restart period; the Seller is not liable for associated delay damages or penalties to the extent this clause lawfully applies. Unaffected obligations and accrued payments continue unless mandatory law provides relief. If disruption exceeds the completed threshold, either party may terminate the affected unperformed portion by written notice. Reconcile delivered goods and refund advances for undelivered goods less only sums lawfully due, without double recovery. Mandatory impossibility, hardship and judicial-adjustment rules remain unaffected.

14. Safety, Taxes and Compliance. The Buyer must provide suitable licensed vehicles, trained personnel, permits and safe collection instructions, and comply with site rules and product safety information. The Seller may refuse unsafe loading without default. Each party is responsible for its own breach or negligence as required by law. The commercial terms determine taxes and charges. Both parties must comply with applicable trade, sanctions, customs, environmental and safety laws; neither must perform an illegal act.

15. Authority, Law and Complete Agreement. Only an authorised Seller representative may agree to a variation, credit, warranty or delivery guarantee in writing. This Contract is the entire agreement for the order. The completed governing-law and court fields apply subject to mandatory rules. The parties will first seek good-faith resolution without delaying urgent relief or timely filing. Failure to enforce a right is not a waiver; invalid provisions are severed only as law allows. Counterparts and electronic or scanned signatures may be used where legally valid.
